name: Max Stoiber
category: Open-source engineer / startup founder (styled-components, Spectrum, Stellate)
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created styled-components with Glen Maddern in October 2016 (~age 22), a CSS-in-JS library that became a default React styling approach with massive adoption.
early_history_summary: Austrian JavaScript engineer who shipped popular React OSS (including react-boilerplate) and co-created styled-components in 2016 while working in open source (Thinkmill). Shortly after co-founded Spectrum (acquired by GitHub), later founded Stellate (acquired by Shopify), then engineering leadership at Shopify and OpenAI.
family_context_summary: Austrian background (Dornbirn/Vienna references); detailed parental professions/wealth not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: styled-components, React OSS wave, Spectrum cofounder, GitHub/Shopify network
evidence_summary: Stoiber co-created styled-components in Oct 2016, a foundational CSS-in-JS library with tens of thousands of GitHub stars and very large npm adoption. He then co-founded Spectrum (GitHub acquisition) and later Stellate (Shopify acquisition). Early advantage is OSS skill plus complementary collaborators and the React componentization wave more than documented family capital. Birth year 1994 is CSV-supplied and consistent with 2016–2017 career timing but not independently vital-record confirmed.
starting_point: Born ~1994 in Austria; early path through JavaScript/React open source rather than a well-documented elite family or institutional pipeline.
current_position: Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI; previously Shopify engineering director after Stellate acquisition; co-creator of styled-components.

trajectory.event: Co-created styled-components with Glen Maddern, popularizing CSS-in-JS for React.

name: Sebastian McKenzie
milestone_by_age_26: Created 6to5 (later Babel) in September 2014 at age 17 while still in Australian high school; the project became the dominant ES6+ JavaScript compiler ecosystem tool.
early_history_summary: From Wodonga, Australia; built websites from age 8 and shipped amateur products as a teen. First-committed 6to5 on 28 Sep 2014 while studying for final exams; project exploded via simple docs/REPL. Hired at Thinkmill at 17, then Cloudflare/Facebook; later co-created Yarn and founded Rome (Biome lineage).
family_context_summary: Regional Australia (Wodonga); family details sparse; self-described social anxiety and high-school adversity in his 2015 review essay.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen OSS, ES6 wave, high-school compiler, Thinkmill/Facebook, open-source distribution
evidence_summary: McKenzie's own 2015 essay documents creating 6to5 at 17, finishing high school without university exams, and converting OSS traction into a Thinkmill job then big-tech roles. Babel's industry-wide adoption makes this one of the clearest ≤26 independent-engineer milestones in JS tooling. Advantage stack is intense self-directed practice and structural ES6 demand, not elite institutions or family capital.
starting_point: Born ~1997 in regional Australia (Wodonga); self-taught web/OSS path from childhood without university pipeline.
current_position: JavaScript tooling engineer known for Babel, Yarn, and Rome/Biome lineage; left Facebook and continued independent/tooling work.

trajectory.event: Pushed first 6to5 commit (later Babel) during final year of high school in Australia.
Hired by Thinkmill in Sydney after cold-emailing with 6to5 traction.
Project rebranded to Babel; joined Cloudflare then Facebook to work on JS tooling.
Co-created Yarn package manager at Facebook with collaborators.
Left Facebook and advanced Rome (later Biome ecosystem lineage) as next-gen tooling.

name: Henry Zhu
milestone_by_age_26: Became primary community maintainer of Babel after Sebastian McKenzie stepped back (~2016–2017, ~age 23–24), then went full-time on Babel via community funding—sustaining a critical JS infrastructure project.
early_history_summary: Entered Babel via formatting/docs contributions, then progressively took on maintenance as the founder moved on. Transitioned from day-job employment to full-time Open Collective–funded Babel maintainership, becoming the public face of Babel's sustainability era.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Babel succession, Open Collective, maintainer sustainability, JS tooling network
evidence_summary: Zhu's material by-26 milestone is assuming primary Babel maintainership in the mid-2010s and making that role viable full-time—critical infrastructure work, not a greenfield invention of Babel itself. Confidence on exact birth year is medium (CSV 1993); career timing still places the succession inside age ≤26 under that year. Family background largely undocumented.
starting_point: Not documented in detail; rose through open-source contribution rather than a public elite-family narrative.
current_position: Long-time Babel maintainer and open-source sustainability advocate; public face of community-funded JS infrastructure maintenance.

trajectory.event: Stepped into primary Babel maintenance as founder attention shifted away.
Became full-time community-funded Babel maintainer via Open Collective sustainability model.
Widely profiled as exemplar of open-source maintainer funding and burnout tradeoffs.
